newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola futures end up on crushers.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola futures end up on crushers.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher on crusher and export demand, traders said.

"Crushers bought 650 July late and at least 200 August. Commission houses sold new crop with Cargill buying," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to +3.15 Wednesday from -2.09 Tuesday. RBC-DS sold July-Nov spread at $31. Volume was 5,500 lots, or 110,000 tonnes.
Japan bought 4,000-5,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
July canola rose $3 to close at $405.10 and November settled up $2.50 at $374.20.
July flax rose $2 to close at $333. September lost $1 to end at $323 as commercial buying met hedges and November settled up $2.30 at $322.50.

July western barley ended up $1 at $133.10 as commission houses and Louis Dreyfus Corp bought from Alberta Wheat Pool and UGG. October rose $0.80 to $134.60, a trader said. About 100 July-Oct spread at $1.50. Volume was 1,125 lots.
July feed wheat rose $1.20 to end at $159.70 as XCan bought and locals sold December up $1.80 to $160.80 to commercials, traders said. AWP sold 85 July-Dec spread $1.
Cargill sold 10 October feed pea contracts up US$0.50 to US$186 to commercials, traders said.
Commercials traded 10 July oats contracts up the US$5 a tonne limit at US$120 a tonne.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
